title: Magic Hall
tagline: A candlelit home for art, music, and their stories.

project_story_sections.Inspiration: Images and songs can lose their meaning when they become files in a folder. I wanted a place to enjoy a work and return to the idea that started it. Magic Hall brings art, music, and their origins into a candlelit room.
project_story_sections.What it does: Gold candles open pictures. Blue candles play music. Visitors can change the picture or track, control playback, and open the story behind a work. The public demo includes newly created sample media and clearly labeled fictional conversations, so the full experience can be explored without my personal collection.
project_story_sections.How we built it: Magic Hall began on November 17, 2026, during the hackathon. Kiro Crew designed and coded the original application, guided by my goals and visual feedback. It uses HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, and Canvas 2D. The public edition loads local JSON and bundled media, with no application backend or runtime AI service.
project_story_sections.Challenges we ran into: The main design challenge was making a magical space understandable. Candle colors needed to explain the controls while leaving the artwork and music at the center. Preparing a self-contained public collection also required separating the application's behavior from private media and source links.
project_story_sections.Accomplishments that we're proud of: A complete visit takes only a few actions: enter the hall, choose a candle, enjoy a work, and revisit its origin. The original application was accepted for my own use. I especially value keeping a creative work connected to the moment that inspired it.
project_story_sections.What we learned: An interface can preserve context as well as display content. The candle theme helps visitors choose a medium, while the origin story gives a work another layer of meaning. Kiro translated concrete creative direction and feedback into working browser interactions.
project_story_sections.What's next for Magic Hall: Future work could make it easier to assemble a personal collection and attach a short origin note to each work, while preserving the calm, deliberate experience of choosing what to view or hear.

category_fit: The candlelit theme explains the application. Gold candles hold pictures and blue candles hold music. Choosing a candle reveals a creative work, and its associated story returns the visitor to the idea behind it. The magical atmosphere gives different media a shared place to explore.
how_kiro_was_used: Kiro Crew designed and coded the original Magic Hall application from November 17, 2026. I provided the goal, aesthetic direction, and feedback: a magical room with gold candles for pictures, blue candles for songs, and a way to return to the conversation behind a work. Codex assisted with the original background and content preparation. The public adaptation was prepared with ChatGPT/Codex assistance from November 20. Its documentation distinguishes that adaptation from the original Kiro work and identifies the actual dates and contributors.
new_project_and_reuse_disclosure: The submitted Magic Hall application was started during the hackathon on November 17, 2026. The idea grew from an earlier personal creative archive. The earlier archive infrastructure is not presented as new hackathon work. The public edition has its own small sample collection, with asset origins and licenses documented in the repository.
public_demo_asset_disclosure: The public demonstration contains newly created sample artwork and instrumental audio, plus fictional conversations. It does not include my private image library, personal songs, or real conversations. The asset manifest identifies the tools, generation methods, attribution, and distribution terms of the bundled assets.
judge_instructions: Open the application URL in a modern browser.
Select a gold candle to open an artwork and use the picture control to discover another sample.
Select a blue candle to play an instrumental sample; try pause, volume, and track selection.
Open the source or story control to read the fictional conversation associated with a work.
Close the overlay and return to the hall.
